---
title: "Tutorial: re-docking a cyclic peptide"
---

{{< include /_includes/adcp-1.0-banner.md >}}

This tutorial re-docks a cyclic peptide with a disulfide bond into its native receptor: a 10-mer
peptide from EBV into HLA-A*11:01 ([PDB 5GRD](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/5GRD)).

**You will learn to:**

- generate a target file for docking in a box defined by the known peptide
- run ADCP to re-dock a cyclic peptide
- understand the output of an ADCP docking run

**Prerequisites:** ADFRsuite 1.0 installed with `ADFRsuite-1.0/bin` on your `PATH`, and the
[tutorial data](https://ccsb.scripps.edu/adcp/download/1063/) downloaded
(see [Tutorials](tutorials.qmd)).

## 1. Generate the target file

Go to the directory for this tutorial:

```bash
cd ADCP_tutorial_data/5GRD
```

This tutorial starts from PDBQT files. See the [first tutorial](tutorial-redocking.qmd) for
converting PDB files to PDBQT.

```bash
agfr -r 5GRD_recH.pdbqt -l 5GRD_pepH.pdbqt -o 5GRD
```

## 2. Dock the cyclic peptide

```bash
adcp -t 5GRD.trg -s sscsscplsk -N 20 -n 500000 -cys -o 5GRD_redocking -ref 5GRD_pepH.pdbqt -nc 0.8
```

Two options are added compared with the linear peptide:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-cys` | enables the potential for disulfide bonds |
| `-nc 0.8` | clusters by native contacts; recommended for larger peptides |

The run writes:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `5GRD_redocking_ranked_*.pdb` | final solutions, ranked after clustering |
| `5GRD_redocking_*.pdb` | the Monte Carlo trajectory of each replica |
| `5GRD_redocking_*.out` | detailed output of each replica |

::: {.callout-important}
Docking cyclic peptides is very hard. This tutorial only shows how to use ADCP; for production
runs, use more replicas with more Monte Carlo steps.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Review note (prototype only)
The example output says "20 ADCP runs with 5000000 steps each", but the command uses
`-n 500000`. One of the two is wrong on the CCSB page.
:::
